title: California's 22nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 22nd Congressional District pits incumbent Republican David Valadao against Democratic challenger Randy Villegas. Valadao, a dairy farmer and former state assemblyman, has represented the Central Valley in Congress for six non-consecutive terms and serves on the House Appropriations Committee. Villegas, a progressive political science professor at College of the Sequoias and Visalia Unified School Board trustee, advanced from the top-two primary by defeating moderate Democrat Jasmeet Bains. Redistricting prior to this election made the district more competitive; as of June 2026, Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated the race a Toss-up, while Inside Elections rated it Tilt Republican. This battleground contest will test whether Valadao's cross-party appeal can withstand a well-funded progressive challenge in a district with a large Latino and working-class population.
polling_note: The only available poll is a top-two primary poll conducted before the June 2 primary, including both Democratic candidates (Villegas and Bains). No general-election head-to-head polls were found as of mid-June 2026.

candidates.name: David Valadao
candidates.summary: David Valadao is the incumbent Republican representative for California's 22nd Congressional District, first elected in 2012 (with a single-term defeat in 2018). He is a lifelong Central Valley resident, dairy farmer, and serves on the House Appropriations Committee. Valadao has focused on agriculture and water policy and has positioned himself as an independent-minded conservative who has periodically broken with party leadership.

candidates.name: Randy Villegas
candidates.summary: Randy Villegas is a Democratic candidate for California's 22nd Congressional District. He is a professor of political science at College of the Sequoias and a trustee on the Visalia Unified School District Board of Education. Raised in a working-class immigrant family in Bakersfield, he became the first in his family to earn a Ph.D. and has campaigned as a progressive, rejecting corporate PAC money and focusing on healthcare, education, and working-class issues. He advanced from the top-two primary by defeating moderate Assemblymember Jasmeet Bains.

forecast.rationale: No general-election head-to-head polling exists as of mid-June 2026; the only available survey was a pre-primary poll (Data for Progress, May 2026) that tested the Democratic primary matchup only. The forecast therefore relies on non-polling indicators: outside race ratings (Cook/Sabato: Toss-up; Inside Elections: Tilt Republican), incumbency advantage for Valadao (six non-consecutive terms and known cross-party appeal in a competitive Central Valley district), and the nature of the Democratic challenger. Villegas advanced past a moderate Democrat in the top-two primary by running as a progressive, which could energize the base but may be a slight liability in a district with a large Latino and working-class electorate where Valadao has demonstrated crossover appeal. Redistricting made the district more competitive, and the challenger is well-funded and credible, keeping the race close. With zero general-election polls, confidence is low, but Valadao's incumbency, fundraising network, and history of surviving tough races give Republicans a narrow edge consistent with a Tilt Republican rating.
